title: BMD BLE camera payload profile
description: Validates payloads/models/<MODEL_KEY>/ble/<FIRMWARE>.json files at load time (camera_profile.validate_profile). Every protocol value in a profile must originate from a sniffer capture on that exact camera/firmware — see CLAUDE.md design principle 6 and docs/ble/payload_profiles.md.

ble_name.description: Real BLE advertisement name broadcast by the camera — not a placeholder.

status.description: Whole-profile status. VERIFIED only after testing every populated section on real hardware. Per-command verification lives in commands.<name>.provenance.status.

characteristic_incoming.description: Only present when overriding the default INCOMING_CONTROL UUID in constants.py.

capabilities.description: Explicit capability model (CLAUDE.md design principle 7), e.g. supports_raw / supports_photo / supports_playback. Populate only once confirmed on the camera.

commands.description: One block per sniffer-confirmed command family (recording, photo, playback, ...), keyed by command name.

codecs.description: Codec name -> {id, variants} lookup consumed by the codec_quality command family. Sniffer-sourced per model — see docs/settings.md.

resolutions.description: Resolution label -> {width, height, codecs, dimension_enums} lookup consumed by the video_format and recording_format command families. Sniffer-sourced per model — see docs/settings.md.

fps_modes.description: FPS label (e.g. "23.98") -> {fps_int, m_rate, frame_flags} lookup consumed by the video_format and recording_format command families. Sniffer-sourced per model — see docs/settings.md.

storage.description: Per-camera storage-monitoring signals (CLAUDE.md design principle 10). Same command-block shape as `commands`, but nothing under here is ever sent by this repo's code — these are decode-only hints for notifications the camera emits unprompted.

dataType.description: Symbolic name matching protocol/types.py DataType (official spec coding: VOID/BOOL=0, INT8=1, INT16=2, INT32=3, INT64=4, STRING=5, FIXED16=128). BOOL is an alias of wire code 0 — the spec's 'void/boolean'. INT16_ARRAY (0x82) is NOT official coding — a CANDIDATE wire byte reported on POCKET_6K_G2 v7.9's recording_format packet, see docs/settings.md.

reserved.description: Header byte 3 as captured. Defaults to 0x00 when absent, but real cameras deviate (POCKET_6K_G2 v7.9 recording uses 0x01) — always record the captured value.

operation.description: Command operation byte. Absent means ASSIGN (0x00), the only operation observed on controller-issued commands so far.

values.description: Named payload values, e.g. {"start": 2, "stop": 0}. Names are what code and the discovery tool address; integers are the sniffer-captured payload bytes. Optional, for two reasons: a multi-element command family (codec_quality, video_format, recording_format) composes its payload from the top-level lookup tables (codecs/resolutions/fps_modes) instead, and a VOID trigger family has no payload at all — both omit this map.

echo_operation.description: Operation byte the camera uses when reporting this category/parameter on INCOMING_CONTROL (0x02 CAMERA_REPORT on every capture so far). Raw integer so an unknown future value still round-trips.

storageSignal.description: A passively-decoded storage-monitoring notification. Same shape as `command` minus the send-only fields (reserved, operation, echo_operation) — nothing under `storage` is ever sent by this repo's code.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset within the payload that carries the signal. Most storage signals will use 0 (the leading byte); a signal may need a nonzero offset when earlier bytes are constant/unexplained on every capture seen so far.

values.description: Named payload values, e.g. {"nominal": 1, "low_margin": -2}. Only the exact values actually observed on the wire — never a sign-based or range-based generalization (CLAUDE.md design principle 6).

codecSpec.description: One codec family: its wire id (codec_quality payload element 0) and named quality variants (payload element 1). Variant ids are per-codec — BRAW's 0 (Q0) and ProRes's 0 (HQ) are unrelated.

resolutionSpec.description: One resolution: pixel dimensions (recording_format payload), the codec families the camera offers at it, and the per-codec video_format dimension_enum values. A codec listed in `codecs` without a `dimension_enums` entry means the camera supports the combination but its enum has not been captured yet.

codecs.description: Codec names (keys of the top-level `codecs` table) offered at this resolution.

dimension_enums.description: Codec name -> video_format dimension_enum byte. The enum encodes resolution AND codec family together, so it is keyed per codec.

known_unreachable.description: Codec name -> evidence note, for a (codec, resolution) pair the camera demonstrably supports (confirmed reachable through its own body menu) but that this codebase's writes cannot reach over BLE OUTGOING_CONTROL despite exhausting every write-value hypothesis (resolution, fps, data type, operation, codec variant, all confirmed correct) — see docs/settings.md. This is a software capability gap, not a camera capability gap: never remove the codec from `codecs` above for an entry listed here. CameraSession.set_camera_format raises BMDUnsupportedError immediately, before any write, for a (codec, resolution) pair listed here.

max_fps_int.description: The highest fps_modes.<name>.fps_int this resolution supports at all, on the camera itself — a genuine hardware/sensor-readout ceiling (unlike known_unreachable, which is a software write-path gap for a combination the camera CAN do). Real example: POCKET_6K_PRO v8.6's '6K' resolution tops out at 50 — 59.94/60fps aren't offered by the camera's own UI at 6K for any codec, confirmed operator-side, not just absent from a write's echo (docs/settings.md). Absent means no known ceiling (every fps_modes entry is assumed available). CameraSession.set_video_format/set_recording_format raise BMDUnsupportedError immediately for a fps whose fps_int exceeds this, before any write.

fpsModeSpec.description: One frame-rate mode: the integer fps byte shared by video_format and recording_format, the video_format m_rate flag (0 exact, 1 NTSC/drop), and the recording_format int16 frame_flags value.

status.description: Per-command verification state: VERIFIED = confirmed on real hardware, CANDIDATE = discovered but awaiting a repeat confirmation, UNVERIFIED = copied/assumed (should not normally exist — sniff instead).
